title: Projection base change at common coefficients
statement:
Fix a finite field $k_0$ of characteristic $p$, an algebraic closure $k$ of $k_0$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$, an integer $n\ge1$, and an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ containing $E$. Let $S$ be a six-functor datum at these coefficients [def-sf-datum], with the specified operation and comparison data [def-fix-six-functor-datum].

Work at $\Lambda=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ in the common finite-stage categories $D^b_c(T,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$ [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients].

Let
$$\begin{array}{ccc}
X'&\xrightarrow{g'}&X\\
f'\downarrow&&\downarrow f\\
Y'&\xrightarrow{g}&Y\end{array}$$
be a Cartesian square of finite-type $k$-schemes. Assume $f$ is separated, and supply a compactification $c=(j:X\hookrightarrow\overline X,p:\overline X\to Y)$ with $j$ open, $p$ proper and $pj=f$, together with its Cartesian base change $c'=(j',p')$; all squares and factorizations are part of the specified compactified square. No separatedness of $g$ or of the structure morphisms is assumed. Write $U_u=Lu^*$, $F=Rf_!^c$, $F'=Rf'_!^{c'}$, and $P_f(K,L)=\operatorname{PF}_{f,K,L}^c$, using the datum's recorded projection components [def-sf-constructible-projection-mates, def-exchange-projection]. Let $e_M:U_gFM\to F'U_{g'}M$ be the specified compact-support exchange, with only the datum's endpoint identifications. Let $\mu_u(A,B):U_u(A\otimes B)\xrightarrow{\sim}U_uA\otimes U_uB$ be the canonical normalized tensor-pullback comparison [def-pur-completed-pullback-tensor-comparison], and let $\kappa_L:U_{g'}U_fL\xrightarrow{\sim}U_{f'}U_gL$ be the inverse pullback compositor to $U_{fg'}L$, transport through $fg'=gf'$, then the pullback compositor to $U_{f'}U_gL$. Tensor and pullback at $R$ are completed, at $E$ rationalized, and at $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ represented over a common finite field. For the inputs specified below, the following equality holds:
$$\begin{aligned}
F'\bigl((1\otimes\kappa_L)\circ\mu_{g'}(K,U_fL)\bigr)\circ e_{K\otimes U_fL}\circ U_g(P_f(K,L))
={}&P_{f'}(U_{g'}K,U_gL)\circ(e_K\otimes1)\circ\mu_g(FK,L).
\end{aligned}$$
Both sides have source $U_g(FK\otimes L)$ and target $F'(U_{g'}K\otimes U_{f'}U_gL)$, using exactly the specified maps, rather than independently chosen isomorphisms.

Here $K\in D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$ and $L\in D^b_c(Y,\Lambda)$ are arbitrary; no extra second-input Tor hypothesis is imposed.

Verbatim retained old parent argument, in source order:
Choose $f=pj$ and its Cartesian base change; by [def-exchange-projection] $\operatorname{PF}^c=R(\gamma_j)\pi_p$ and $\operatorname{Ex}_!^c=R'(\beta)e$. Apply [lem-sf-pf-open-base-change-square] with $M=j_!K$, $Q=M\otimes FL$: it supplies all completed constructible domains, monoidality of $\theta:F'G\cong HF$, and the open-factor equality. The ordinary adjunctions are [fix-prop-adjunctions](1). The proper exchange $e$ is their specified mate of $\theta$ by [def-exchange-projection, fix-lem-exchanges], and $\pi_p$ is the counit projection. Apply [lem-sp-categorical-projection-mate-square] with its adjunctions $Lp^*\dashv Rp_*$, $Lp'^*\dashv Rp'_*$, $N_D=G$, $N_C=H$, $\alpha=\theta$, $\varphi=\mu_F$, $\varphi'=\mu_{F'}$, $m_C=\mu_H$, $m_D=\mu_G$; its hypothesis ComparisonCompatible is the monoidality equation just cited. Its conclusion is $R'(d)e_QG(\pi_{p;M,L})=\pi_{p';HM,GL}(e_M\otimes1)\mu_{G;RM,L}$ with $d=(1\otimes\theta_L^{-1})\mu_H$, the proper-factor hypothesis of [lem-sf-pf-compactification-pasting]; the open one is the equality above. That pasting identity gives the displayed square: its target comparison is $La^*JFL\cong J'HFL\to J'F'GL\cong Lf'^*GL$. Refinement compatibility and square naturality in [fix-lem-exchanges](1),(4), with projection compatibility from step 1, remove the compactification choice; the naturality clause of the pasting lemma gives naturality in the morphism data. At finite coefficients apply [lem-sf-finite-base-change-transport]: its proof identifies each constructible-coordinate route under faithful realization, substitutes the existing fixed-scalar diamond equality, cancels the common target isomorphism, and reflects equality through the full inclusion. This retains the proper/open mate calculation and adds no separatedness of the horizontal map.

Exact sorried source theorem header:
theorem sixFunctorProjection_baseChange_common (S : SixFunctorDatum D C E n hn) :
    ∀ (Q : SixFunctorCompactifiedSquare D)
      [IsSeparated Q.f.hom.left]
      (K : generalAlgebraicallyClosedConstructibleCategory C.l C.Qbar Q.X.obj.left)
      (L : generalAlgebraicallyClosedConstructibleCategory C.l C.Qbar Q.Y.obj.left),
      (S.closure.commonStage.pull Q.g).map ((S.closure.commonStageExchange Q).projectionComponent
        K L) ≫
        sixFunctorProjectionExchange (S.closure.commonStageExchange Q)
          (((S.closure.commonStageTensor Q.X).obj K).obj ((S.closure.commonStage.pull Q.f).obj L)) ≫
        (S.closure.commonStage.support Q.f' Q.compactification').map
          ((sixFunctorProjectionCommonMu S Q.g' K
            ((S.closure.commonStage.pull Q.f).obj L)).hom ≫
            ((S.closure.commonStageTensor Q.X').obj ((S.closure.commonStage.pull Q.g').obj K)).map
              (((S.closure.commonStage.pullComposition Q.g' Q.f).inv.app L) ≫
                eqToHom (congrArg
                  (fun f ↦ (S.closure.commonStage.pull f).obj L) Q.squareComm) ≫
                (S.closure.commonStage.pullComposition Q.f' Q.g).hom.app L)) =
      (sixFunctorProjectionCommonMu S Q.g
        ((S.closure.commonStage.support Q.f Q.compactification).obj K) L).hom ≫
        ((S.closure.commonStageTensor Q.Y').map
          (sixFunctorProjectionExchange (S.closure.commonStageExchange Q) K)).app
            ((S.closure.commonStage.pull Q.g).obj L) ≫
        (S.closure.commonStageExchange (compactSupportProjectionSquare Q.f'
          Q.compactification')).projectionComponent
          ((S.closure.commonStage.pull Q.g').obj K) ((S.closure.commonStage.pull Q.g).obj L)

proof.text:
First establish the open-factor equation for arbitrary common-stage $K$ on $X$ and $P$ on $\overline X$. Its completed integral version follows from [lem-sf-pf-open-base-change-square] applied to the compactification $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{1}\overline X$, base changed along $h$. The required integral second input is any bounded constructible integral $P_0$: [lem-coef-integral-residue-tor] supplies its uniform finite-reduction Tor interval. Thus, at every finite coefficient field $E_0$ with valuation ring $R_0$, for arbitrary integral $K_0,P_0$, that cited node gives
$$z^0_{K_0,P_0}H_0(\gamma^0_{j;K_0,P_0})=\gamma^0_{j';A_0K_0,H_0P_0}(\beta^0_{K_0}\otimes1)\mu^0_{H; j_!K_0,P_0},$$
where $z^0=j'_!((1\otimes\sigma^0)\mu^0_A)\beta^0$. This equality is of completed arrows before finite evaluation. The auxiliary proper map is the identity, and the cited open-square theorem permits arbitrary $h$; it requires no absolute separatedness.

proof.text: Choose one finite coefficient field $E_0$ representing $K,P$ in the pair category [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. Its raw rational category has the same objects as its integral category [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], so choose integral objects $K_0,P_0$ representing them. Let $C_W$ be rationalization followed by inclusion into the common-stage category on each scheme $W$. Use only the prescribed operation endpoints $c_B:C_W(B_0)\cong B$ for each expression in the open equation. The higher-coefficient clause of [def-exchange-projection] defines $\beta,\gamma$ by rationalization and common-field classes, with scalar comparisons intertwining the open adjunction units and the pullback compositors; [def-sf-operation-stages] specifies these same open, pullback and composition comparisons. The tensor and pullback comparison is precisely the normalized common-field representative in [def-pur-completed-pullback-tensor-comparison], and [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso] gives its scalar and composition compatibility. Consequently each constituent arrow $r_0:B_0\to D_0$ in step 2 represents the actual arrow $r=c_D C(r_0)c_B^{-1}$, including $\mu_A,\mu_H,\sigma,\beta,\gamma$ and their functor images. These are not newly chosen tensorators or endpoint automorphisms.

proof.text:
Apply the functors $C_W$ to the equality of step 2 and substitute the constituent-arrow formulas of step 3. Adjacent endpoints cancel: $(c_D C(s)c_B^{-1})(c_B C(r)c_A^{-1})=c_D C(sr)c_A^{-1}$. Thus both sides have the same outer endpoints, and one obtains, for the original $K,P$,
$$z_{K,P}H(\gamma_{j;K,P})=\gamma_{j';AK,HP}(\beta_K\otimes1)\mu_{H;M,P},\qquad z_{K,P}=j'_!((1\otimes\sigma_P)\mu_{A;K,JP})\beta_{K\otimes JP}.$$
Changing the common representative leaves the same morphism class, by the tower and identity comparisons specified in step 3. In particular apply this with $P=F_pL$. This uses preservation of an equality by functors, not faithfulness of finite reductions or of coefficient inclusion.

proof.text:
At common coefficients the composition compatibility in [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso], applied to the actual equality $p h=g p'$, gives the monoidality of $\theta:F_{p'}G\cong HF_p$. Explicitly, for $B,C$ on $Y$,
$$\mu_{H;F_pB,F_pC}\,H(\mu_{F_p;B,C})\,\theta_{B\otimes C}=(\theta_B\otimes\theta_C)\,\mu_{F_{p'};GB,GC}\,F_{p'}(\mu_{G;B,C}).$$
Indeed both sides are the composite-map tensor comparison for $ph=gp'$, read through the specified two pullback compositors. This is exactly ComparisonCompatible in [lem-sp-categorical-projection-mate-square], with adjunctions $F_p\dashv R_p$, $F_{p'}\dashv R_{p'}$, horizontal functors $G,H$ and $\alpha=\theta$. The proper exchange $e$ and the proper projection $\pi$ are the mate and counit projection specified in [def-exchange-projection]. Apply the categorical lemma at $M,L$. With $d=(1\otimes\theta_L^{-1})\mu_{H;M,F_pL}$ it gives
$$R_{p'}(d)e_QG(\pi_{p;M,L})=\pi_{p';HM,GL}(e_M\otimes1)\mu_{G;R_pM,L}.$$
Only the ordinary adjunctions of the supplied stage are used; no adjunction or separatedness assumption on $g,h$ is needed.
